Computing ${B}^{2},$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{B}^{2} & =B\cdot B \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2 & -4 \\ 1 & -2\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}2 & -4 \\ 1 & -2\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0\end{aligned}] \\  & =O.\end{aligned}
$$

Notice that, since ${B}^{2}=O,$ the matrix $B$ is a nilpotent matrix of index $2.$ 

We can use this fact to compute ${B}^{3}$ quickly, as follows: 

$$
\begin{aligned}{B}^{3} & ={B}^{2}\cdot B \\  & =O\cdot B \\  & =O\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,  

$$
{B}^{3}=[\begin{aligned}0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0\end{aligned}].
$$
